findings.what: The claim that a current I through R₁ and R₂ in series makes a voltage I(R₁ + R₂) has no source in this lesson's sources or checks; research notes 5.5 hold it (LibreTexts 21.1: V = IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃ = I(R₁ + R₂ + R₃)), so add that source and a K.check that cites it.

The screen goes straight from 'takes away the whole bracket' to 'so every sign inside changes' and leaves out the link the explain text gives (a lone minus is −1 times the bracket, so each term is multiplied by −1; taking away 5 less than 6x gives 5 back), so add one clause on screen.

'The order cannot show a minus in front of a bracket' is too absolute, because 8x − (6x − 5) m (cutting a piece 5 m short of 6x off an 8x m drum) is a positive length that cable can show; say it cannot show a lone −(6x − 5) or a negative total.
The winding of 2.0 Ω cold and 2.4 Ω after a run is an assumed example but is not called one on this screen, while step 8 says 'these example values'; write 'an example winding'.
